IBM.rationale: IBM presents a quality-improving incumbent story with genuine but modest positive momentum. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): YoY revenue growth of +9.5% and EPS growth of +14.3% in Q1 2026 are solid for a mature enterprise IT firm, and cash conversion is exceptional at 4.2x (OCF $5.17B vs net income $1.22B). However, Q1 2026 standalone operating margin of only 8.7% is thin and raises questions about TTM margin durability (TTM operating margin of 15.3% is inflated by a strong Q2 2025 quarter). Balance sheet leverage at 3.7x liabilities/equity is elevated. Revenue growth of 9.5% lags the peer average of 12.43% and net margin of 7.64% trails competitors. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE has compressed dramatically from ~50x in late 2025 to 23.4x, now near the low of its 19-51x range. P/B compressed from 10.8x to 7.6x. This is meaningful improvement, but the earnings yield of 4.3% barely exceeds the 10Y Treasury at 4.45%, offering essentially no equity risk premium. The re-rating has largely occurred already. Pillar 3 (catalyst): The CHIPS Act quantum foundry announcement (2026-05-21) with $1B federal backing and $1B IBM investment, plus the $10B through-2029 quantum commitment, is a genuine strategic catalyst that drove a ~17% stock surge. However, quantum revenue remains negligible and the payoff horizon extends to 2029. The Q1 2026 earnings beat ($1.91 adjusted EPS vs $1.81 consensus) and dividend increase to $1.69/quarter (31-year streak) provide modest additional support. Net: improving trajectory and a meaningful strategic catalyst offset by thin margins, elevated leverage, no equity risk premium, and a catalyst whose earnings impact is years away. Score of +0.25 reflects mildly attractive fundamentals with a modest catalyst bump.
